title: Module 2: Qualifying Clients
nextTeaser: Next, Module 3 goes deeper into discovery and shows how the OneAccord community helps you serve the client.

blocks.html:
Module 2 of 5. Learn to qualify thoroughly up front so we only pursue right-size, right-time, right-fit clients. Don't always be closing. Always be qualifying.

Here's how this module works: watch the video, work through a few short sections, answer a quick knowledge check, respond to a scenario (your coach grades it, and 3 of 4 points passes), then build one piece of your personal Sales Game Plan.

blocks.html:
1. Right fit over winning

  • Right fit matters more than winning. A square peg in a round hole "fits," but it leaves gaps around the edges.
  • Capacity isn't only budget. It's also time, energy and people. A client without capacity turns an engagement into frustration for both sides.
  • "Ears to hear": will the owner receive hard truths delivered with compassion?
  • "You can't manufacture pain." If the need or timing isn't there, keep them in the pipeline and wait for their season. Don't want it more than they do.

2. Right-size clients

Annual revenueFit
$25M+Our focus today
Under $25MAn exception, not the rule. We still take on a few smaller clients, so qualify carefully and involve your managing principal early.

Look at the bottom line, not just the top line. A $30M company losing money may not be able to invest.

3. BANT, with questions to ask

What you're confirmingTry asking
BudgetCan they invest, based on the bottom line?"Have you set aside resources to solve this?" · "What has this problem cost you over the past year?"
AuthorityWho decides, and who else must agree (partners, board, spouse)?"Who else would be involved in a decision like this?" · "How have you made similar decisions before?"
NeedIs it a need-to-have or a nice-to-have? Is there real pain?"What happens if nothing changes in the next 12 months?" · "Why now?"
TimingIs this their season? It might be 3 weeks, 3 months or 3 years out."Is there a deadline or event driving this?" · "What else competes for your attention this year?"

4. Red flags beyond BANT

From the Sales Playbook, watch for:

  • No identifiable value we can create
  • You can't reach the real decision-maker
  • Unclear decision criteria or decision process
  • Pain the owner won't name
  • No internal champion
  • No critical event creating urgency

Several red flags you can't resolve means it's time to disqualify (Module 4 covers how).

5. BANT, then B.U.Y.E.R.S.

BANT happens up front, before you invest real time. Once a prospect qualifies, you track their progress through the B.U.Y.E.R.S. Journey (covered in depth in Module 5). A prospect who isn't Bothered (who can't name the problem and has no sense of urgency) isn't an opportunity yet.

blocks.prompt: A $30M company wants to engage but is losing money. What's the main concern?
options: The top line fits, but the bottom line may not support the investment
Unprofitable companies are never a fit
There's no concern if the owner is motivated
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. Budget is about the bottom line, not just revenue.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: The concern is the bottom line: the top line fits, but they may not be able to invest.

blocks.prompt: A prospect has $12M in revenue and a clear need. What's the right approach?
options: Pursue it like any other deal
Qualify carefully: it's below our $25M+ focus, so involve your managing principal before investing much time, or refer them
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Smaller clients are exceptions, so bring in your managing principal early.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Smaller clients are exceptions. Qualify carefully and involve your managing principal early, or refer them.

blocks.prompt: What does "you can't manufacture pain" mean?
options: If the need and timing aren't there, you can't create them. Wait for their season
Create urgency in the first meeting
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Exactly. Keep them in the pipeline and wait for the right season.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: It means you can't create need or timing. Keep them in the pipeline and wait for their season.

blocks.prompt: The owner loves the idea but says his two partners "would need to weigh in." Which BANT element needs work?
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. You need to understand who decides and how.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: It's Authority. The partners are part of the decision.

blocks.promptHtml:
A well-known local company ($60M, profitable) is interested in working with us. They've replaced their CFO four times in ten years, and leadership has a reputation for not taking advice. A colleague is eager to pursue them.

Walk through BANT and decide what to do.
rubric: Works through BANT explicitly and notes that budget and size check out
Identifies the 'ears to hear' / leadership receptiveness risk, using the CFO turnover as a signal
Names what they'd need to learn or test before investing more time
Reaches a clear decision (pursue with conditions, wait, or decline) with reasoning

OneAccord focuses on $25M+ revenue companies; a few smaller clients are exceptions, so qualify carefully and involve a managing principal early. BANT: Budget (bottom line, not just top line; a $30M company losing money may not be able to invest), Authority (who decides, and who else must agree: partners, board, spouse), Need (need-to-have vs nice-to-have; real pain; 'you can't manufacture pain'), Timing (right season: 3 weeks, 3 months or 3 years). Capacity is also time, energy and people. 'Ears to hear': will leadership receive hard truth delivered with compassion? Red flags from the playbook: no identifiable value, can't reach the decision-maker, unclear decision criteria or process, pain the owner won't name, no internal champion, no critical event. Keep good-but-not-ready prospects in the pipeline; don't want it more than they do. BANT comes first; qualified prospects are then tracked through the B.U.Y.E.R.S. Journey (Bothered = can identify the problem and expresses urgency).

blocks.title: Qualify a Live Prospect
blocks.promptHtml: Pick one real prospect (you can anonymize the name). Run them through BANT honestly. It's fine to write "unknown" and flag what you still need to learn.

fields.label: Prospect (industry, approximate size, how they came to you)
What you know for Budget, Authority, Need and Timing
The next 3 questions you'll ask them, and your call: pursue, wait or refer

criteria: Each BANT element is addressed honestly, with gaps flagged rather than assumed
Red flags are considered, not skipped
The next questions are open-ended and specific to this prospect
There is a clear pursue / wait / refer decision with a reason (and a managing principal involved if under $25M)
